<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par145" />{{GHGmargin-letter|145|n}}
'''6'''. Subjects in the dual are construed with the plural of the predicate, since verbs, adjectives, and pronouns, according to {{GHGpar|88|a}}, have no dual forms; thus {{GHGheb|text=עֵינַ֫יִם}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=29|verse=17}} {{GHGheb|text=וְעֵינֵי לֵאָה רַכּוֹת}} ''and Leah’s eyes were dull''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=24|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=30|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=14|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=7|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=38|verse=11|hidebook=1}} (on the other hand, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=4|verse=15}} the predicate is in the feminine singular ''after'' the subject, and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=4|verse=11}} ''before'' it; on both constructions cf. ''k'' above); so also {{GHGheb|text=אָזְנַ֫יִם|translate=ears}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=6|verse=40}}; {{GHGheb|text=יָדַ֫יִם|translate=hands}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=10|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=20|verse=10|hidebook=1}} (in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=17|verse=12}} even with the plural masculine {{GHGheb|text=כְּבֵדִים}}; cf. ''p''); {{GHGheb|text=שְׂפָתַ֫יִם|translate=lips}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=1|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=27|verse=4}}; {{GHGheb|text=שָׁדַ֫יִם|translate=breasts}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=9|verse=14}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|145|o}}
'''7.''' Variations from the fundamental rule (see above, ''a'') very frequently occur ''when the predicate precedes the subject'' (denoting animals or things<ref>Only rarely does an uninflected predicate precede a personal subject, as {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=25|verse=27}} (but {{GHGheb|text=הֵבִ֫יאָה}} should probably be read, as in verse 35); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=9|verse=23}} (before a plur. masc.). Such examples as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=42|verse=15}} are to be explained according to {{GHGpar|121|a}}.</ref>). The speaker or writer begins with the most simple form of the predicate, the uninflected 3rd singular masculine, and leaves us without indication as to which of the following subjects (and so which gender or number) is to define the predicate thus left temporarily indefinite.<ref>In a certain sense this is analogous to the German ''es kommt ein Mann, eine Frau'', &c.</ref> Thus inflexions are omitted in—

(''a'') The verb, with a following singular feminine, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=2|verse=17}} {{GHGheb|text=וְשַׁח גַּבְהוּת הָֽאָדָם|translate=and bowed down shall be the loftiness of man}}; 9:18, 14:11, 28:18, 47:11; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=25|verse=27}} (see note 1 below); {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=8|verse=31}}<sup>''b''</sup>, 22:36, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=3|verse=26}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=51|verse=46}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=7|verse=7}}; with a following plural masc., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=13|verse=22}} {{GHGheb|text=וְעָנָה אִיִּים|translate=and there shall cry wolves}}, &c.; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=13|verse=17}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}}, 20:46, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=1|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=4|verse=10|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=24|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=13|verse=33}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=51|verse=48}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=124|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=9|verse=23}} (see note 1 below); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=1|verse=14}} {{GHGheb|text=יְהִי מְאֹרֹת|translate=let there be lights}}; with a following plural feminine, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=35}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=11|verse=3}}<sup>''a''</sup>, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=8|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=13|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=2|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=57|verse=2}}; before collectives and mixed subjects, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=12|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=13|verse=5|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=30|verse=43|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=32|verse=6|hidebook=1}}, &c.; before a following dual, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=44|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=73|verse=7}} (where, however, with the LXX {{GHGheb|text=עֲוֹנָ֫מוֹ}} should be read).

{{GHGmargin-letter|145|p}}
Rem. 1. The instances in which a preceding predicate appears in the plural masculine before a plural (or collective singular) feminine of persons ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=21|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=11|verse=3}}<sup>''b''</sup>), of animals ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=30|verse=39}} where however {{GHGheb|text=צאֹן}} may refer specially to male animals) or of things ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=26|verse=33}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=13|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=14|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=16|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=3|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=6|verse=9}}), or before a dual ({{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=4|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zp|chapter=3|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=15|verse=7}}) are to be explained not on the analogy of the examples under ''o'', but from a dislike of using the 3rd plur. fem. imperf., for this is the only form concerned in the above examples (cf., however, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=3|verse=11}} {{GHGheb|text=תְּהִי}} instead of {{GHGheb|text=תִּֽהְיִי}}); cf. the examples of a following predicate in the 3rd plur. masc., instead of the fem., under ''t'' and ''u'', and on an analogous phenomenon in the imperative, see {{GHGpar|110|k}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|145|q}}
2. As in the case of verbs proper so also the verb {{GHGheb|text=הָיָה}}, when used as a copula, frequently remains uninflected before the subject; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=5|verse=23 ff.}}, 39:5,<section end="par145" /><noinclude>
